diagnosis: All four rollouts successfully revealed both PF1 and PF2 and cited PF2 in justification_fact_ids, so there is no disclosure or telepathy problem. The sole failing check is C7, which passed only in rollout 1 and failed in rollouts 0, 2, and 3. The difference is the commitment type encoding: rollout 1 used a standalone commitment with type "record_attachment" ("Attach the QC report confirming the 88-minute approved DCP to the programming record"), while rollouts 0 and 2 bundled the attachment requirement into a "master_file" commitment (e.g., "Use the approved 88-minute festival cut DCP as the screening master for panorama, and attach Elise's QC report to the programming record"), and rollout 3 omitted the attachment mention entirely from its "master_file" commitment. This is an ENCODING MISMATCH: C7 appears to require a specific commitment type (likely "record_attachment" or similar) to recognize the ingest-record/QC-report attachment update, but models naturally fold that requirement into a "master_file" commitment most of the time.

C7.why: The ingest QC result changes screening_runtime_minutes from the catalog draft's 94 to exactly 88, selects an approved festival-cut DCP, and requires an ingest-record or QC-report attachment update.
